Topics · Is the Quran from God?

How did the Quran's first listeners react?

The Quran records hostile and moved reactions; tradition reports one heart almost flew. What does this show?

Part 1 of 3

﴿وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ لَا تَسْمَعُوا۟ لِهَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْءَانِ وَٱلْغَوْا۟ فِيهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَغْلِبُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And those who disbelieve say, "Do not listen to this Qur’ān and speak noisily[1391] during [the recitation of] it that perhaps you will overcome."

Translator's notes

[1391] Other meanings include "speak improperly" and/or "make a clamor." The purpose of this was to prevent the hearing or understanding of the Qur’ān.

Quran · Fussilat 41:26

﴿وَإِذَا تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَايَـٰتُنَا قَالُوا۟ قَدْ سَمِعْنَا لَوْ نَشَآءُ لَقُلْنَا مِثْلَ هَـٰذَآ ۙ إِنْ هَـٰذَآ إِلَّآ أَسَـٰطِيرُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And when Our verses are recited to them, they say, "We have heard. If we willed, we could say [something] like this. This is not but legends of the former peoples."

Quran · Al-Anfal 8:31

A book that won everyone at once would invite suspicion. This one records, in its own pages, how some of its first hearers reacted: they told one another not to listen and to make noise over the recitation, and they said they had heard it and could say the like if they wished. The book keeps its critics' words in its text. That is a point about the book's candour in reporting what was said about it.

A question for you

What can a hostile reaction tell you about a text?

If you sayThat it was taken seriously.
ThenThat is one fair reading. It is a modest one: it says the text was heard, not that it was right.
If you sayNothing about whether it is true.
ThenAgreed. Reactions, hostile or warm, do not settle truth. They only tell you what happened when it was heard.
If you sayThat it unsettled something.
ThenPerhaps. What it unsettled is for each hearer to say. The next part looks at the other kind of reaction the book records.

Part 2 of 3

﴿بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ قُلْ أُوحِىَ إِلَىَّ أَنَّهُ ٱسْتَمَعَ نَفَرٌ مِّنَ ٱلْجِنِّ فَقَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّا سَمِعْنَا قُرْءَانًا عَجَبًا١ يَهْدِىٓ إِلَى ٱلرُّشْدِ فَـَٔامَنَّا بِهِۦ ۖ وَلَن نُّشْرِكَ بِرَبِّنَآ أَحَدًا٢﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, [O Muḥammad], "It has been revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened and said, 'Indeed, we have heard an amazing Qur’ān [i.e., recitation]. It guides to the right course, and we have believed in it. And we will never associate with our Lord anyone.

Quran · Al-Jinn 72:1-2

﴿وَإِذَا سَمِعُوا۟ مَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَى ٱلرَّسُولِ تَرَىٰٓ أَعْيُنَهُمْ تَفِيضُ مِنَ ٱلدَّمْعِ مِمَّا عَرَفُوا۟ مِنَ ٱلْحَقِّ ۖ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَآ ءَامَنَّا فَٱكْتُبْنَا مَعَ ٱلشَّـٰهِدِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth. They say, "Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses.

Quran · Al-Ma'idah 5:83

The Quran records the other reaction too: a group of jinn who heard it and said it was a wonderful recitation that guides to what is right, and people whose eyes overflowed with tears at what they recognised in it. Notice that these are reports inside the book itself. They do not prove where it came from. They show the kind of effect the book says it has: not only argument, but recognition.

A question for you

What does it mean to you when a text moves people?

If you sayThat it touches something real.
ThenMany would say so. The weight you give it is yours to decide.
If you sayThat it is well made, nothing more.
ThenA fair view. Many texts move people. This one is offered here as one sign among others, not as a proof.
If you sayThat people who are moved are not judges of truth.
ThenAgreed, and the Step does not treat them as such. The next part is one report, with its limit stated.

Part 3 of 3

﴿أَمْ خُلِقُوا۟ مِنْ غَيْرِ شَىْءٍ أَمْ هُمُ ٱلْخَـٰلِقُونَ٣٥ أَمْ خَلَقُوا۟ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ ۚ بَل لَّا يُوقِنُونَ٣٦﴾

Translation of the meaning

Or were they created by nothing, or were they the creators [of themselves]? Or did they create the heavens and the earth? Rather, they are not certain.

Quran · At-Tur 52:35-36

Translation

I beg you, my child, to lift your eyes to the sky and the earth, and to see all things that are in it, and thus to recognize that God made them not of things that were, and that the race of men in this way comes into being.

Original · Ancient Greek

Ἀξιῶ σε, τέκνον, ἀναβλέψαντα εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν, καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτοῖς πάντα ἰδόντα, γνῶναι ὅτι ἐξ οὐκ ὄντων ἐποίησεν αὐτὰ ὁ Θεὸς, καὶ τὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων γένος οὕτως γεγένηται,

2 Maccabees · 7:28

World English Bible

Take the question in this verse. Were you created from nothing, or are you your own creator? It does not need Arabic or any faith to feel its weight, and listeners who were not believers could be struck by exactly such a question. It may strike you differently, or not at all. Ask what your own answer is, and notice how quickly or slowly it comes.

A question for you

Which sounds closer to what you would feel if you heard that question for the first time?

If you sayCuriosity: I would want to hear the answer.
ThenThat is where the verse itself goes next. It lists the possibilities and leaves the last one to you.
If you sayUnease: it is a hard question.
ThenIt is, and it is meant to be. Another Step takes it slowly and gives you time.
If you sayIndifference: it has no hold on me.
ThenThat is an honest answer, and no one is asked to feel more than they feel.

The same in the other books

Translation

Know that Yahweh, he is God. It is he who has made us, and we are his. We are his people, and the sheep of his pasture.

Original · Hebrew

דְּע֗וּ כִּֽי־יְהוָה֮ ה֤וּא אֱלֹ֫הִ֥ים הֽוּא־עָ֭שָׂנוּ וְל֣וֹ אֲנַ֑חְנוּ עַ֝מּ֗וֹ וְצֹ֣אן מַרְעִיתֽוֹ׃

the Psalms · 100:3

World English Bible

Your reflection

Think of something you heard once that you have never been able to put down. Why do you think it stayed?
